'contact' is the single place to change who receives course and sponsorship email (name, email, title shown next to the address). 'draft.enabled' adds a visible notice, a noindex/nofollow meta tag, and a robots.txt that disallows crawling; set it to false when the content is final.
name: Metal2Humanoid
tagline: Building a Humanoid Robot from the Ground Up
description: Metal2Humanoid is a proposed non-credit MIT IAP 2027 course: a four-week, hands-on introduction to humanoid robotics, from motors and actuators to coordinated motion and learned behavior, built on an open-source humanoid.

status.approvalNote: Proposed as a non-credit MIT IAP 2027 activity; approval, meeting times, and rooms are provisional.

hbrn.name: Homebrew Robotics Network
hbrn.relationship: Metal2Humanoid is organized by its instructors together with members of the Homebrew Robotics Network (HBRN), the builder community behind the initiative.
hbrn.blurb: The Homebrew Robotics Network is a community of builders working toward open, accessible, reproducible robotics: hardware that can be built from widely available parts, documented well enough for others to repeat, and shared under open licenses. For Metal2Humanoid, HBRN hardware contributors lead the robot design and the Week 1 actuator materials, and the instructors lead the simulation, locomotion, and task weeks.
hbrn.next: The immediate next step is a v1 humanoid that goes beyond Berkeley Humanoid Lite, built around commercial actuators. Its design will be committed once sponsorship is in place, so that partner hardware can shape it; it is not a course deliverable. Further out, HBRN is exploring two companion efforts that may extend the course materials: OSH Atlas, an atlas of open humanoid projects and resources, and UMOJA, a framework for assessing and comparing open humanoid designs, both possible future extensions for documentation, resource sharing, and benchmarking.
